purpose: Fixed six-candidate retrospective screen before considering a new prospective paper study. Not a change to the installed app or existing studies.
hypothesis: Less frequent 15-minute trend entries with volatility-scaled exits may retain positive returns after realistic and doubled trading costs.
source: Official Binance spot ZIP archives with published SHA-256 checksums
window_integrity: Parameters fixed before downloading outcomes for this experiment. These market dates overlap observation by other studies; neither period is asserted to be untouched independent data. All become development evidence after inspection. No fitting or re-ranking variants on the later window.
cost_breakdown: Per side: fee 10 bps, half-spread 2 bps, slippage 5 bps. Stress doubles all components. Assumptions, not measured historical order books.
execution: Existing opportunity audit: finalized-bar signals; next continuous opening entry; stop first on ambiguous bars; adverse opening gaps honored; expiry precedes target on final allowed bar; one non-overlapping position per candidate; no shorts or leverage.
boundary_handling: Each period is scored independently with no carried position. Unresolved tail/gap outcomes are excluded and counted, never fabricated; any censored or missing-data outcome prevents advancement in this screen.
screen_gate: For BOTH periods: at least 100 completed trades, positive base and stressed average, at least 10 distinct exit dates, positive Bonferroni-adjusted one-sided 95% lower bound of equally weighted daily average stressed trade returns (12 comparisons), no missing bars, no invalid archive boundary rows, no gap or tail-censored trades. This diagnostic lower bound is not a calibrated trading-success probability; no live qualification.
survivor_action: Retain every candidate; only survivors may be proposed for a separately registered prospective paper protocol. Never change the frozen studies, enable qualified alerts, place orders, or infer a profitable live service from this screen.
repeat_policy: One retained attempt; data/network/calculation failures remain recorded. Any retry uses a new attempt identity and cannot erase failed attempts. No parameter optimization in this round.
